answer:
**Natural-language hypothesis (data-grounded, descriptive only):**

"Among individuals who were ever incarcerated (ever_jailed==1, 1985–1994), median 1985 wealth was very low overall — about $720, roughly one-fifth of the $3,600 median among never-incarcerated respondents — and exhibited systematic demographic disparities. There is a clear racial gradient: ever-incarcerated White respondents had a median 1985 wealth around $2,200, versus about $320 for Black and $0 for Hispanic respondents (White-to-Black point-ratio ≈ 7:1; White-to-Hispanic ≈ 4.5:1), with White–Black and White–Hispanic differences reaching significance in rank-based tests (p ≈ 0.047 and 0.041). This disparity is concentrated at the bottom of the wealth distribution: roughly 39% of ever-incarcerated Black males and 42% of Hispanic males had exactly zero 1985 wealth, versus ~21% of White males; once zero-wealth records are excluded, group medians converge to roughly $3,000–$5,500 across races/ethnicities, indicating the racial gap reflects a higher mass of Black and Hispanic ever-incarcerated individuals with no (or negative) wealth rather than lower wealth among those holding any assets. By sex, ever-incarcerated females had a median of $0 versus $1,000 for males (median difference $1,000, bootstrap 95% CI $260–$1,400; p ≈ 0.024). Together, the largest and most reliable disparity is the male-vs-female gap (all else held equal, median wealth for men exceeds that of women by ~$1,000 and the CI excludes 0) and the White-vs-Black/Hispanic ordering driven primarily by the much higher prevalence of zero wealth among Black and Hispanic ever-incarcerated individuals. These are descriptive associations only: wealth is measured in 1985 while the incarceration window spans 1985–1994, so no causal ordering is implied."

Supporting main table (median 1985 wealth among ever-jailed, n=289):
| race × sex | n | median (95% CI) | median excl. zeros |
|---|---|---|---|
| white male | 57 | 2,000 (400–5,200) | 5,000 |
| black male | 143 | 800 (0–1,400) | 3,350 |
| hipanic male | 52 | 700 (0–3,000) | 5,475 |
| white female | 12 | 4,100 (0–20,700) | 7,200 |
| black female | 16 | 0 (0–0) | 3,100 |
| hipanic female | 9 | 0 (0–0) | 700 |

Race-only: white 2,200 (n=69) > black 320 (n=159) > hipanic 0 (n=61). Sex-only: male 1,000 (n=252) > female 0 (n=37). Background: jailed 720 (n=289) vs non-jailed 3,600 (n=11,724). Zero-wealth share among jailed: white male 21.1%, black male 39.2%, hipanic male 42.3%; female cells 78–81% for black/hispanic vs 33% for white (chi2 p=0.029 race-within-males; p=0.001 by sex).

payload.hypothesis: Among ever-incarcerated individuals, 1985 median wealth is very low overall (~$720, ~1/5 of the ~$3,600 non-incarcerated median) with systematic demographic disparities: a racial ordering White (~$2,200) > Black (~$320) > Hispanic (~$0) driven mostly by a higher zero-wealth incidence among Black/Hispanic (39-42% vs 21% for White males), and a sex gap male ($1,000) > female ($0; CI $260-$1,400) that is the most statistically reliable contrast.
payload.workflow: 1) Inspected data (12,013 obs, 6 cols, no missing). 2) Defined ever incarcerated via ever_jailed==1. 3) Computed median composite_wealth_1985 among ever-jailed by race, sex, and race x sex with 4,000-resample bootstrap 95% CIs; reported n per cell. 4) Estimated pairwise median differences with bootstrap CIs; added Mann-Whitney U tests and chi-square tests of zero-wealth incidence. 5) Sensitivity: repeated medians excluding zero-wealth records. 6) Wrote a natural-language hypothesis focusing on within-incarcerated demographic disparities, flagged small female cells (n=9-16) and kept interpretation descriptive (wealth 1985 vs 1985-1994 incarceration window).
